candidates.source_description:
A Roman sculpture of a Satyr seizing a nymph found at Tivoli, Italy and now located in the British Museum, London.

Date: 100-200AD

https://www.britishmuseum.org/collection/object/G_1805-0703-2

67 photos taken in November 2023 with a Sony a7R III and processed in Reality Capture.
candidates.subject: sculpture
candidates.title: Satyr and Nymph (Townley group)
candidates.dimensions: height 75 cm, width 64 cm, depth 48 cm
candidates.scan_source: Independent photogrammetry (67 photos, Reality Capture) published on Sketchfab
candidates.note: Roman marble group of a nymph struggling to escape a satyr, found near Tivoli and acquired by Charles Townley; restored in the 18th century by the sculptor Sposino, including the nymph's head. One of several copies of a Hellenistic work of the 2nd or 1st century BCE, among them a near-complete twin in the Capitoline Museums, Rome. The British Museum once kept it in its restricted Museum Secretum (M466) and now catalogues the scene as probable sexual violence.

candidates.source_description:
**CAT:** Figura grotesca, segurament la representació de Príap, déu de la fecunditat, de la qual devien penjar campanetes (tintinabulum). MNAT 542. Bronze. I dC. (16,5 x 8 x 10 cm). 

**ES:** Figura grotesca, seguramente la representación de Príapo, dios de la fecundidad, de la cual colgarían campanillas (tintinabulum). MNAT 542. Bronce. I dC. (16,5 x 8 x 10 cm). 

**EN:** Grotesque figure probably depicting Priapus, the god of fertility, from which small bells (tintinabulum) would have hung. MNAT 542. Bronze. 1st century AD. (16,5 x 8 x 10 cm).

candidates.source_description:
**CAT:** Fal·lus que pren la forma d’una estatueta, amb la representació de Príap. Segurament elaborada en un taller local, no se’n coneix cap d’igual. MNAT 518. Marbre. I - II dC. (34 x 13 x 12,5 cm).

**ES:** Falo que toma la forma de una estatuilla, con la representación de Príapo. Seguramente elaborada en un taller local, no se le conoce ningún paralelo. Mármol. I - II dC. (34 x 13 x 12,5 cm).

**EN:** Phallus in the form of a small statue representing Priapus. Probably made in a local workshop. It is the only one of its kind known. Marble. 1st – 2nd centuries. (34 x 13 x 12,5 cm).

Model 3D optimitzat per M. Mercè Grau Salvat sobre model de Global Digital Heritage
